ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A car is traveling at a constant speed of $36\mathrm{km/h}$ on a straight road. Starting from a certain moment, it accelerates with an acceleration of $0.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. At the end of 10 seconds, it suddenly brakes and comes to a stop. The deceleration during braking is $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the speed of the car at the end of 10 s?
2. The distance a car travels from braking to coming to a complete stop

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A car is traveling at a constant speed of $36\mathrm{km/h}$ on a straight road. Starting from a certain moment, it accelerates with an acceleration of $0.5\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. At the end of 10 seconds, it suddenly brakes and comes to a stop. The deceleration during braking is $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. What is the speed of the car at the end of 10 s? 2. The distance a car travels from braking to coming to a complete stop
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given values: initial speed is 36 km/h, acceleration for the first 10 s is 0.5 m/s^2, and braking deceleration is 10 m/s^2. First convert the initial speed: 36 km/h = 36 × 1000 / 3600 = 10 m/s. After accelerating for 10 s, use v = u + at: v = 10 + 0.5 × 10 = 15 m/s. This is the speed at the end of 10 s and also the initial speed when braking begins. For the braking distance, final speed is 0, initial speed is 15 m/s, and acceleration is -10 m/s^2. Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as: 0^2 = 15^2 + 2(-10)s, so 0 = 225 - 20s, hence s = 225/20 = 11.25 m.
